sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》庆祝成立175周年，持续助您理解世界，过好每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，享受nyt.com斜杠subscribe的特别优惠。

sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: Hurricane Otis, which killed more than two dozen people in southern Mexico this week, has revealed a new kind of threat that meteorologists fear will become more and more common.
sentences.zh: 飓风奥蒂斯本周在墨西哥南部造成数十人死亡，它揭示了一种气象学家担忧将变得越来越普遍的新型威胁。

sentences.en: A severe hurricane that arrives with shockingly little warning or time to prepare.
sentences.zh: 一场伴随着令人震惊的极少警告或准备时间而至的严重飓风。

sentences.en: My colleague Judson Jones explains.
sentences.zh: 我的同事贾德森·琼斯为您解析。

sentences.en: It's Friday, October 27th.
sentences.zh: 今天是10月27日，星期五。

sentences.en: Judson, we're coming to you because you are a meteorologist on the staff of The Times, which is a pretty new development, I have to think,
sentences.zh: 贾德森，我们来找你是因你是《时报》员工中的气象学家，我想这算是一个相当新的动态，

sentences.en: because I didn't actually know that The Times had a meteorologist on our staff.
sentences.zh: 因为我之前其实并不知道《时报》员工里有一位气象学家。

sentences.en: So I came on about a year ago, last Halloween, and it all came about because The Times wanted to develop an extreme weather team.
sentences.zh: 所以我大约是一年前、也就是去年万圣节前后加入的，这一切的起因是《时报》想要组建一个极端天气团队。

sentences.en: We often say extreme weather is the fingerprint of climate change.
sentences.zh: 我们经常说极端天气是气候变化的指纹。

sentences.en: So a lot of times it's the evidence that the world is changing.
sentences.zh: 所以很多时候，它是世界正在发生改变的证据。

sentences.en: And so by bringing on a meteorologist and a data journalism team, my team is responsible for diving into the data of these extremes.
sentences.zh: 因此，通过引入气象学家和数据新闻团队，我的团队负责深入研究这些极端天气的数据。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So the reality that climate change and extreme weather are deeply interwoven is why you are at The Times.
sentences.zh: 所以，气候变化与极端天气深度交织这一现实，正是你来到《时报》的原因。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Well, let's turn to the reason we're talking to you right now, which is an extreme weather event that happened just a couple of days ago, Hurricane Otis,
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们转向我们现在找你谈话的原因，也就是就在几天前发生的一场极端天气事件——飓风奥蒂斯，

sentences.en: and why it felt so different to those of us watching it than most hurricanes.
sentences.zh: 以及为什么在我们这些旁观者看来，它与大多数飓风感觉如此不同。

sentences.en: What made Otis so remarkable and scary was that it rapidly intensified from a tropical storm Tuesday morning to a Category 5 hurricane by nightfall.
sentences.zh: 奥蒂斯之所以如此引人注目又可怕，是因为它在周二早上的热带风暴状态下迅速增强，到入夜时分已达到5级飓风强度。

sentences.en: Basically, it went from your run-of-the-mill storm to the most terrifying, powerful, destructive kind of hurricane in less than 24 hours.
sentences.zh: 基本上，它在不到24小时内，就从一场平平无奇的风暴变成了最可怕、最强大、最具破坏力的飓风。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, it was the ultimate nightmare scenario.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是终极的噩梦场景。

sentences.en: So tell us the full story of Otis from the beginning, from your perspective as somebody watching it.
sentences.zh: 那么请从你的角度，作为一名观察者，给我们讲讲奥蒂斯从头到尾的完整故事。

sentences.en: Well, in full transparency, on Wednesday morning, I woke up and went, what happened?
sentences.zh: 好吧，坦白说，周三早上我醒来时的第一反应是：发生了什么？

sentences.en: Like, normally, we have a lot of lead-up time to hurricanes, right?
sentences.zh: 就像，通常我们在飓风来临前有很多准备时间，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, we're tracking them across the Atlantic Ocean.
sentences.zh: 比如，我们在大西洋上追踪它们。

sentences.en: We're tracking them across the Pacific Ocean.
sentences.zh: 我们在太平洋上追踪它们。

sentences.en: You can see them coming.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到它们在靠近。

sentences.en: It gives the forecast models time to initialize and give different results over, you know, a couple of days.
sentences.zh: 这给了预报模型时间去初始化，并在几天内给出不同的结果。

sentences.en: So there's this chance to kind of understand that the storm is coming here.
sentences.zh: 所以大家有机会意识到风暴正朝这里驶来。

sentences.en: This storm...
sentences.zh: 这场风暴……

sentences.en: Otis is new to the scene in the eastern Pacific.
sentences.zh: 奥蒂斯是东太平洋的新面孔。

sentences.en: This is a tropical storm...
sentences.zh: 这是一场热带风暴……

sentences.en: ...formed on Sunday.
sentences.zh: ……形成于周日。

sentences.en: It was 40 miles per hour.
sentences.zh: 当时风速为每小时40英里。

sentences.en: Otis is pushing its way towards Acapulco.
sentences.zh: 奥蒂斯正朝着阿卡普尔科逼近。

sentences.en: So we're going to see some very heavy rain around the southwest of Mexico.
sentences.zh: 所以墨西哥西南部将会迎来一些非常大的降雨。

sentences.en: On Monday, it was 50 miles per hour.
sentences.zh: 周一时，风速为每小时50英里。

sentences.en: The forecast models weren't really showing it intensifying at all.
sentences.zh: 预报模型并没有显示它有任何增强的迹象。

sentences.en: Tropical storm Otis continues to spin in the eastern Pacific.
sentences.zh: 热带风暴奥蒂斯继续在东太平洋旋转。

sentences.en: Wings right now 45 miles.
sentences.zh: 目前风速为45英里。

sentences.en: Tuesday morning, it was still a tropical storm.
sentences.zh: 周二早上，它仍然是一场热带风暴。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So around 50 miles per hour.
sentences.zh: 所以风速大约在每小时50英里。

sentences.en: But by midday, it was 80 miles per hour.
sentences.zh: 但到了中午，风速达到了每小时80英里。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: It was a Category 1 hurricane strength.
sentences.zh: 它达到了1级飓风的强度。

sentences.en: It started to look even more like a hurricane on satellite, which kind of gives an indication that it's intensifying.
sentences.zh: 从卫星上看，它看起来越来越像个飓风了，这某种程度上预示着它正在增强。

sentences.en: An eye started to form.
sentences.zh: 开始形成风眼。

sentences.en: Now let's talk about this one in the Pacific.
sentences.zh: 现在我们来谈谈太平洋上的这个家伙。

sentences.en: This thing just jumped up just to a Category 3.
sentences.zh: 这家伙一下子就跃升到了3级。

sentences.en: And then that afternoon, hurricane hunters flew through the eye twice and found that it was actually a Category 4 strength hurricane.
sentences.zh: 然后那天下午，飓风猎人飞机两次穿过风眼，发现它其实已经达到了4级飓风的强度。

sentences.en: Now we go to a potentially dangerous situation developing in Mexico.
sentences.zh: 现在我们转向墨西哥正在发展的一个潜在危险情况。

sentences.en: A rapidly intensifying hurricane is making its way toward the resort community of Acapulco.
sentences.zh: 一场迅速增强的飓风正朝度假胜地阿卡普尔科驶去。

sentences.en: And then later that night, all of a sudden, it was 165 miles per hour.
sentences.zh: 然后那天深夜，转眼间，风速达到了每小时165英里。

sentences.en: The strongest storm that has ever hit the west coast of Mexico.
sentences.zh: 这是有史以来袭击墨西哥西海岸的最强风暴。

sentences.en: So every hour or every two hours, this thing is becoming like an entire order of magnitude bigger.
sentences.zh: 所以每隔一个小时或两个小时，这家伙就以数量级的规模在变大。

sentences.en: And that's just not, you're saying, normal.
sentences.zh: 而你说，这根本不正常。

sentences.en: You know, it's one of the fastest strengthening storms we've ever experienced.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是我们经历过的增强速度最快的风暴之一。

sentences.en: It is beyond the definition of rapid intensification.
sentences.zh: 它已经超出了“急剧增强”的定义。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: The typical definition is 35 miles per hour in 24 hours.
sentences.zh: 典型的定义是在24小时内风速增加35英里每小时。

sentences.en: This one went above 100 miles per hour in 24 hours.
sentences.zh: 而这个家伙在24小时内风速增加了100多英里每小时。

sentences.en: Like it jumped from a tropical storm to a Category 5.
sentences.zh: 就像它从一场热带风暴直接跳跃到了5级。

sentences.en: I mean, it's juSt...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这简直……

sentences.en: Unheard of.
sentences.zh: 前所未闻。

sentences.en: It's remarkable in meteorology terMs.
sentences.zh: 用气象术语来说，这太不可思议了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So when this very anomalously intensifying storm arrives on the western coast of Mexico as a Category 5 storm,
sentences.zh: 那么，当这场异常增强的风暴作为5级风暴抵达墨西哥西海岸时，

sentences.en: describe for us what happens, given the fact that from everything you're saying, there hasn't been very much time at all to prepare.
sentences.zh: 请为我们描述一下发生了什么，考虑到你所说的一切，根本没有多少准备时间。

sentences.en: The winds came in howling.
sentences.zh: 狂风呼啸而至。

sentences.en: I mean, they were ripping off palm leaves, and you can see it in video before all the power cut off.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它们把棕榈树叶都撕扯下来了，在断电前的视频里你就能看到这一点。

sentences.en: Then all of a sudden, you know, these tourists and the residents, there are nearly a million people who live in the city, had broken, shattered windows.
sentences.zh: 然后突然间，你知道，这些游客和居民——这座城市里居住着近百万人口——的窗户都被砸碎了。

sentences.en: The sides of buildings were starting to rip off.
sentences.zh: 建筑物的侧墙开始被撕裂。

sentences.en: You know, you can see the rain coming into people's bedrooms, you know, where they're trying to sleep.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你可以看到雨水吹进了人们正试图睡觉的卧室里。

sentences.en: I mean, this came in normally when people would be sleeping.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这发生时通常正是人们在睡觉的时候。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I think I remember 1 a.m.
sentences.zh: 我记得大约是当地时间凌晨1点左右。

sentences.en: local time or so.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可以想象一下，你以为自己只要在睡梦中度过风暴就行了，然后突然间窗户就被砸得粉碎。

sentences.en: I mean, you just imagine, like, you think you're just going to sleep through the storm, and then all of a sudden the windows are just being shattered.
sentences.zh: 等到太阳升起时，你知道，手机基站瘫痪了，互联网中断了。

sentences.en: And by the time the sun came up, you know, cell towers were down, internet was down.
sentences.zh: 要弄清楚地面上到底发生了什么非常困难。

sentences.en: It was really difficult to find out what was going on on the ground.
sentences.zh: 但我们现在知道，破坏极其严重。

sentences.en: But we know now that the damage was extensive.
sentences.zh: 已造成27人死亡，还有更多人失踪。

sentences.en: 27 people have died, and more are still missing.
sentences.zh: 这似乎确实突显了急剧增强带来的问题。

sentences.en: Which really would seem to highlight the problem of rapid intensification.
sentences.zh: 你没有时间疏散人员，因此，更多的人丧生了。

sentences.en: You don't have time to evacuate people, and therefore, more people die.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 在这个本应能指望有预报并让人群撤离的现代社会，我们绝不希望看到任何人死于风暴中。

sentences.en: In this modern age where you expect forecasts and people to be able to evacuate, we never want to see anyone die in the storMs.
sentences.zh: 作为气象学家，这就是我们为什么要进行预报。

sentences.en: As meteorologists, like, that's why we forecaSt.
sentences.zh: 是为了拯救生命。

sentences.en: It's to save lives.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切又回到了这场风暴的凶猛程度上。

sentences.en: And so it just goes back to the ferociousness of this storm.
sentences.zh: 鉴于你刚才描述的一切让它显得很不寻常，飓风奥蒂斯究竟有多不寻常？

sentences.en: Just how unusual is Hurricane Otis, given everything you've just described, which makes it feel very unusual?
sentences.zh: 并没有我们希望的那么不寻常。

sentences.en: Not as unusual as we hope.
sentences.zh: 我担心我们将更频繁地看到这种现象发生。

sentences.en: I'm afraid that we're going to see this happen more frequently.
sentences.zh: 你知道，研究表明急剧增强的现象正在更频繁地发生。

sentences.en: You know, studies are showing that rapid intensification is happening more often.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是我们需要做好准备的未来。

sentences.en: I think that's the future we need to prepare for.
sentences.zh: 我们去去就来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜露。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我编写了《纽约时报》游戏中的益智游戏“连线”（Connections）。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我也喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·阿泽斯基，我每天都创作“拼字蜂”（Spelling Bee）和“字母方块”（Letterboxd）游戏。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Azersky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的特质。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像你刚才听到声音的这些人一样。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 访问nytimes.com斜杠games，今天就开始游戏吧。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 贾德森，有什么证据表明像奥蒂斯这样以闪电般速度增强、几乎没有预警的风暴，

sentences.en: Judson, what is the evidence that storms like Otis, that intensify in what feels like lightning speed with so little warning,
sentences.zh: 现在正变得越来越普遍，并不像你希望的那样不寻常？

sentences.en: are now becoming more common and are not as unusual as you would like them to be?
sentences.zh: 你知道，这确实可以归咎于一部分气候变化。

sentences.en: You know, it's one of the things that you can actually attribute to climate change a little bit.
sentences.zh: 比如，有研究表明，台风和气旋——也就是其他海洋盆地的飓风——

sentences.en: Like, there are studies that have shown that typhoons and cyclones, which are just hurricanes in another ocean basin,
sentences.zh: 正在更频繁地急剧增强。

sentences.en: that they're rapidly intensifying more frequently.
sentences.zh: 就在几周前，还有一项专门针对大西洋飓风的研究表明，在变暖的世界中，急剧增强发生的可能性是两倍。

sentences.en: Even a study just a couple weeks ago that focused specifically on hurricanes in the Atlantic showed that in a warming world, rapid intensification is twice as likely to happen.
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，告诉我们这种现象正变得越来越普遍的依据，是人们研究了过去的风暴并指出：这一现实不容否认。

sentences.en: So essentially, the thing that tells us that this is becoming more common is people studying old storms and saying, there's no denying this reality.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，甚至我在过去十年里报道过的风暴，过去偶尔还会让我们觉得，我们会说“这场风暴将会急剧增强”，

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, even the storms I've covered over the last decade kind of used to feel like something we would occasionally say, like, this storm is going to rapidly intensify,
sentences.zh: 或者“那场风暴刚刚急剧增强”。

sentences.en: or that storm just rapidly intensified.
sentences.zh: 而现在感觉几乎我们报道的每一场风暴，都只是又一个这样的迹象。

sentences.en: And now it almost feels like every storm we cover, it's just another indication.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 我想请你用机械原理来解释一下为什么这种增强会发生。

sentences.en: And I want you to just mechanically explain why this intensification is happening.
sentences.zh: 显然，主要的驱动因素是海水温度变暖，但我想请你提醒我们它是如何运作的，以及温暖的海水如何意味着

sentences.en: Clearly, the main driving factor is warming water temperatures, but I want you to just remind us how that works and how a warmer body of water means
sentences.zh: 一场小风暴能如此迅速地变成一场具有巨大破坏力的风暴。

sentences.en: that a small storm is becoming a massive destructive storm so quickly.
sentences.zh: 嗯，要形成飓风，你需要温暖的海水。

sentences.en: Well, to have a hurricane, you need to have warm water.
sentences.zh: 水温必须达到华氏80度或更高，才能真正提供它所需的能量，对吧？

sentences.en: It has to be 80 degrees Fahrenheit or higher to really give it the energy that it needs, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，把飓风想象成一台发动机，而这种能量、温暖的海水就是为飓风提供动力的燃料。

sentences.en: So, think of a hurricane as like an engine, and that energy, that warm water is the fuel that's fueling the hurricane.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，你知道，如果这些风暴在海洋某个区域上空停留很长时间，它们会不断将这些能量抽吸进飓风中。

sentences.en: Typically, you know, these storms, if they sit over an ocean in an area for a long period of time, they continue to pull that energy up into the hurricane.
sentences.zh: 但在下方，较冷的水开始上涌。

sentences.en: But down below, colder water starts upwelling.
sentences.zh: 因此，飓风将正在取代温水的冷水给翻了上来。

sentences.en: So, that hurricane is pooling colder water that's replacing that warm water.
sentences.zh: 但我们在这个变暖的世界中看到的是，变暖的不仅仅是海洋表面温度。

sentences.en: But what we're seeing in this warming world is that it's not just the ocean surface temperatures that are warming.
sentences.zh: 整个水柱都在变暖。

sentences.en: The column of water is warming.
sentences.zh: 所以，没有将较冷的水翻涌进飓风中，它翻涌上来的是更温暖的水，这些水同样在80华氏度以上，从而为风暴提供了更多能量。

sentences.en: So, instead of pooling colder water up into the hurricane, it's upwelling warmer water that is, again, above 80 degrees, which gives more energy to the storm.
sentences.zh: 因此，飓风不会因为失去燃料而渐渐减弱，相反，它正将更多能量汇聚到这场风暴中。

sentences.en: So, instead of a hurricane just kind of petering out because it's lost that fuel, instead, it's pooling more energy into that storm.
sentences.zh: 太迷人了。

sentences.en: That's fascinating.
sentences.zh: 所以，当海洋中为飓风提供的燃料越来越多时，它加速的几率就会越来越高。

sentences.en: So, when there's more and more fuel in the ocean for the hurricane, the chances of it speeding up become higher and higher.
sentences.zh: 它渐渐消散的几率就会越来越小。

sentences.en: The chances of it petering out become smaller and smaller.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So, if you're a meteorologist, which you are, how does this new reality of there being so much warm water fuel for these storms to intensify,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你是一名气象学家（你确实是），面对大量暖水为这些风暴增强提供燃料的新现实，

sentences.en: how does that change your role in warning people about these dangerous storms?
sentences.zh: 这会如何改变你在向人们发出这些危险风暴预警时的角色？

sentences.en: It's almost like we turned back the clock a little bit on forecasting.
sentences.zh: 这简直就像我们在天气预报方面把时钟稍微拨回了一点。

sentences.en: You know, we've come a long way in meteorology, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，气象学已经取得了长足的进步，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, if you think back to the great Galveston hurricane in 1900, they didn't have warning.
sentences.zh: 比如说，如果你回想一下1900年那场毁灭性的加尔维斯顿飓风，当时他们根本没有预警。

sentences.en: And then the satellite era came, and all of a sudden we could see these storms in the Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 后来卫星时代来了，突然之间我们能看到大西洋上的这些风暴。

sentences.en: And we knew that they were going to move towards the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我们也知道它们将向美国移动。

sentences.en: So, we've constantly been improving.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们一直在不断进步。

sentences.en: Forecast models have even gotten better.
sentences.zh: 预报模型甚至变得越来越好。

sentences.en: You know, we have this ability to see a storm out in the Atlantic and say, hey, that may hit the U.S.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们有能力看到大西洋上的风暴，然后说，嘿，它可能会在两周后袭击美国。

sentences.en: in two weeks.
sentences.zh: 在两周内。

sentences.en: However, when you have this rapid intensification equation, right?
sentences.zh: 然而，当你遇到这种急剧增强的方程式时，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, this problem that kind of inserts itself, it kind of changes the game.
sentences.zh: 就像这个问题突然出现一样，它在某种程度上改变了游戏规则。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Kind of undermines all that technology and says to it, you're not up to the task.
sentences.zh: 这在某种程度上颠覆了所有的技术，并对它们说，你们还不够胜任。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I mean, I think scientists are quickly trying to develop
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为科学家们正在迅速尝试开发

sentences.en: better models to predict this intensity because it is a scary thing.
sentences.zh: 更好的模型来预测这种强度，因为这是一件可怕的事情。

sentences.en: I mean, we want to warn people, and it helps to be able to see in the future.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们想要警告人们，而能够预知未来会有所帮助。

sentences.en: Well, what would help you adjust to this pretty scary new reality about faster intensifying storms?
sentences.zh: 那么，有什么能帮助你适应关于风暴增强速度加快这一相当可怕的新现实呢？

sentences.en: What would help you be able to predict that Otis was going to do what it ultimately did?
sentences.zh: 有什么能帮你预测出奥蒂斯会做出最终那样的举动？

sentences.en: Are there some straightforward, easy solutions to that?
sentences.zh: 对此有没有什么直接、简单的解决方案？

sentences.en: I think one thing is better observations.
sentences.zh: 我认为其中一点就是更好的观测。

sentences.en: I think we're getting in an age where we're launching weather satellites all over the place, and that's helping improve our forecasts.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们正进入一个到处发射气象卫星的时代，这有助于改进我们的预报。

sentences.en: Like, having a better understanding of just how intense the storm is ahead of time is key.
sentences.zh: 比如，提前更好地了解风暴究竟有多强是关键。

sentences.en: But even in this situation, it took a hurricane hunter flying through the storm to really know how intense it was.
sentences.zh: 但即便在这种情况下，也需要一架飓风猎人飞机飞入风暴内部，才能真正知道它有多强。

sentences.en: So I think that's one thing, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这是一点，对吧？

sentences.en: But the other thing is the forecaSt.
sentences.zh: 但另一点是预报。

sentences.en: Like, these supercomputers that are trying to predict the future, we need to continue to develop that science.
sentences.zh: 就像那些试图预测未来的超级计算机一样，我们需要继续发展这门科学。

sentences.en: For example, if we had more sensors in the Pacific Ocean, we could get better data and understand what is actually coming from the west to the east or from the east to the west,
sentences.zh: 例如，如果我们能在太平洋中部署更多传感器，就能获得更好的数据，从而了解究竟是什么东西从西向东、或从东向西移动，

sentences.en: depending on what part of the Pacific Ocean you're in.
sentences.zh: 这取决于你身处太平洋的哪个区域。

sentences.en: Like, if we get more data,
sentences.zh: 比如，如果我们获得更多数据，

sentences.en: the forecasts are going to get better.
sentences.zh: 天气预报就会变得更好。

sentences.en: Okay, but even if we get more sensors in the Pacific Ocean, and even if we get better forecasts and better warnings on these more quickly intensifying storms,
sentences.zh: 好吧，但即使我们在太平洋中部署了更多传感器，即使我们对这些增强速度更快的风暴有了更好的预报和预警，

sentences.en: that doesn't solve the problem of helping people on land to prepare when, by definition, they just have less and less time given the warming water.
sentences.zh: 这仍然无法解决帮助陆地上的人们进行准备的问题，因为在水温变暖的情况下，根据定义，他们的时间只会越来越少。

sentences.en: So how are we supposed to solve for that?
sentences.zh: 那我们该如何解决这个问题？

sentences.en: I mean, the straightforward answer would seem to be we need to cut back on emissions, which is clearly a root cause of these warming temperatures,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，最直接的答案似乎是我们必须减少排放，这显然是导致这些变暖气温、

sentences.en: creating these nightmare scenarios.
sentences.zh: 进而造成这些噩梦般场景的根本原因。

sentences.en: But even if we did that, that would take time.
sentences.zh: 但即使我们这样做了，也需要时间。

sentences.en: So what do we do now?
sentences.zh: 那我们现在该怎么办？

sentences.en: If you live in a coastal community and you're getting less and less time to prepare for a hurricane, what can be done?
sentences.zh: 如果你住在沿海社区，而且你准备应对飓风的时间越来越少，能做些什么呢？

sentences.en: A lot of it ends up coming down to mitigation.
sentences.zh: 很多事情最终都要归结为减灾。

sentences.en: It comes down to as simple as building materials.
sentences.zh: 这甚至可以简单到建筑材料的层面。

sentences.en: There are things called hurricane ties that you can get for a few bucks to hold down your roof to the rest of the framework of your house so the roof doesn't blow off.
sentences.zh: 有一种叫作飓风连接件的东西，你花几美元就能买到，用它把屋顶固定在房屋的其余框架上，这样屋顶就不会被吹飞了。

sentences.en: There are things that can be done to help mitigate that disaster.
sentences.zh: 有些事情是可以做来帮助减轻这种灾害的。

sentences.en: Another thing is, you know, not building in floodplains, where we're seeing a lot more of that.
sentences.zh: 另一件事是，你知道的，不要在洪泛区建房，我们现在看到很多这种情况。

sentences.en: But then it's also having shelters readily available that are hurricane-proof or tornado-proof.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，还要随时准备好防飓风或防龙卷风的避难所。

sentences.en: Like, there are things that cities and towns and countries can do to help mitigate the disaster by giving people options if they're in the path of a major storm.
sentences.zh: 比如，城市、城镇和国家可以采取一些措施，为身处强风暴路径上的人们提供选择，从而帮助减轻灾害。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Options that increasingly perhaps need to acknowledge that there might not be time to get in your car and drive for hours and hours.
sentences.zh: 这些选择或许越来越需要承认这样一种现实：可能已经没有时间让你上车并连续开几个小时的车了。

sentences.en: But are contingency plans that perhaps recognize that you may end up needing to stay in your community when one of these storms very rapidly becomes something super dangerous?
sentences.zh: 这些应急计划或许应该认识到，当其中一场风暴迅速变成极其危险的东西时，你最终可能需要留在你的社区里？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: I'm curious, just thinking about the fact that you are a meteorologist, if this situation we're describing makes you feel an immense amount of pressure
sentences.zh: 我很好奇，考虑到你是一名气象学家，我们刚才描述的这种状况是否让你感到了巨大的压力，

sentences.en: to get things righter than ever before.
sentences.zh: 要求你比以往任何时候都更加准确。

sentences.en: I mean, there's always lots of carping when a meteorologist gets something wrong.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当气象学家出错时，总是会有很多挑剔的声音。

sentences.en: You told us to worry about a storm.
sentences.zh: 你让我们担心一场风暴。

sentences.en: It passed us.
sentences.zh: 它从我们身边掠过了。

sentences.en: We're annoyed with you.
sentences.zh: 我们对你感到恼火。

sentences.en: But the burden now feels even more intense because if you're wrong, the amount of time, the room for error, is vanishingly small.
sentences.zh: 但现在的负担感觉更加沉重，因为如果你错了，时间和容错空间就会变得微乎其微。

sentences.en: And the danger is so much greater.
sentences.zh: 而且危险要大得多。

sentences.en: And that puts you in a very tricky position.
sentences.zh: 这把你置于一个非常棘手的境地。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, meteorologists have always gotten it wrong.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，气象学家一直都会出错。

sentences.en: You know, that's why it's a joke because it's a science.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这就是为什么它成了一个笑话，因为它是一门科学。

sentences.en: Meteorologists, what they're doing is creating a hypothesis.
sentences.zh: 气象学家所做的事情是在提出一个假设。

sentences.en: So when they're forecasting, when a meteorologist like myself is giving you a forecast, they're giving their best educated guess based off of everything that's happening around.
sentences.zh: 所以当他们进行预报时，当像我这样的气象学家在给你做预报时，他们是根据周围发生的一切做出自己最有根据的猜测。

sentences.en: So as I write these stories and am trying to forecast these bigger storms, being right is not easy.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我撰写这些报道并试图预测这些更大的风暴时，要做到准确并不容易。

sentences.en: I feel responsible for what people may think by reading those words.
sentences.zh: 我觉得自己对人们读到这些文字时的想法负有责任。

sentences.en: Like, should they evacuate?
sentences.zh: 比如，他们应该撤离吗？

sentences.en: Should they not evacuate?
sentences.zh: 他们不应该撤离吗？

sentences.en: Is this storm actually going to be a big deal?
sentences.zh: 这场风暴真的会是一件大事吗？

sentences.en: And I carry a lot of that weight on my shoulders.
sentences.zh: 我把很多这样的重担扛在肩上。

sentences.en: And in this world where storms can intensify and kind of come out of nowhere, it's not the kind of storm I like to wake up to the next morning and go,
sentences.zh: 在这个风暴会增强且仿佛凭空出现的世界上，这不是那种让我第二天早晨醒来时会说：

sentences.en: oh, I should have covered this two days ago so people had more warning.
sentences.zh: 哦，我应该在两天前就报道这个，好让人们有更多预警的风暴。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I want to be able to warn people three or four days in advance of a major hurricane.
sentences.zh: 我希望能够在强飓风来临前的三四天就向人们发出预警。

sentences.en: And when they rapidly intensify next to a city with nearly a million people, that is the worst nightmare.
sentences.zh: 而当它们在一个拥有近百万人口的城市旁急剧增强时，那就是最大的噩梦。

sentences.en: Well, Johnson, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，约翰逊，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们真的很感激。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来，迈克尔。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: A massive manhunt entered its second day in Maine where police were searching for the gunman who killed at least 18 people at a restaurant and bowling alley
sentences.zh: 缅因州的大规模搜捕行动进入第二天，警方正在搜寻一名枪手，他在一家餐馆和保龄球馆枪杀 了至少18人，

sentences.en: in America's deadliest shooting of the year.
sentences.zh: 这是美国今年最致命的枪击事件。

sentences.en: Police described the suspect as a sergeant first class in the Army Reserve where his superiors became alarmed over statements he had made over the summer, threatening his own unit.
sentences.zh: 警方将嫌疑人描述为陆军预备役的一名一级中士，他的上司曾对他今年夏天发表的威胁自己所在部队的言论感到惊慌。

sentences.en: All Maine people are sharing in the sorrow of the families who lost loved ones last night.
sentences.zh: 所有缅因州人民都在分担着昨晚失去挚亲的家庭的悲痛。

sentences.en: Loved ones,
sentences.zh: 挚亲，

sentences.en: normal people who were killed or injured while unwinding from a day of work or while spending time with their family and friends, socializing.
sentences.zh: 普通人在结束一天的工作放松时，或者在与家人朋友社交聚会时被杀害或受伤。

sentences.en: During a news conference,
sentences.zh: 在一次新闻发布会上，

sentences.en: Maine's governor, Janet Mills, called the shooting a dark day for the state and for the city where it occurred.
sentences.zh: 缅因州州长珍妮特·米尔斯称此次枪击事件对该州以及事发城市来说是黑暗的一天。

sentences.en: I know that the people of Lewiston are enduring immeasurable pain.
sentences.zh: 我知道刘易斯顿的人民正在承受着无法估量的痛苦。

sentences.en: I wish I could take that pain off your hearts, off your shoulders, but I promise you this, we will all help you carry that grief.
sentences.zh: 我希望我能把这种痛苦从你们的心中、从你们的肩上卸下，但我向你们保证，我们会和你们一起分担这份悲痛。

sentences.en: And on Thursday, the Israeli military said it had briefly sent tanks into northern Gaza in preparation for its next stage of fighting, which could involve a ground invasion.
sentences.zh: 周四，以色列军方表示，已短暂派遣坦克进入加沙北部，为下一阶段的战斗做准备，这可能涉及地面进攻。

sentences.en: In Gaza, the Hamas-run health ministry said that the number of Palestinians killed by Israeli airstrikes has surpassed 7,000 people.
sentences.zh: 在加沙，哈马斯运营的卫生部表示，以色列空袭造成的巴勒斯坦人死亡人数已超过7000人。

sentences.en: But those numbers cannot be independently verified and have been questioned by President Biden.
sentences.zh: 但这些数字无法得到独立核实，并受到了拜登总统的质疑。

sentences.en: In response,
sentences.zh: 作为回应，

sentences.en: Hamas released what it said were the names of 6,747 people who had died.
sentences.zh: 哈马斯公布了它所称的6747名死者的名单。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you on Monday.
sentences.zh: 我们周一见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》节目中，我们将为假期接待客人做好准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是深度睡眠者吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they black out to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们喝断片儿才能睡着。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们对光线有什么要求？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》应用程序或你喜欢的任何播客平台上搜索《Wirecutter秀》。

sentences.en: I'd love to see you on Friday.
sentences.zh: 我希望能周五见到你。

sentences.en: See you next week on The Wirecutter Show.
sentences.zh: 下周在《Wirecutter秀》再见。

sentences.en: Bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: I'll see you next time.
sentences.zh: 我们下次再见。
